text:
Talia Benson: Flagging a pilot customer question that keeps coming up in the Terraform alpha rollout. They read “private-only egress” as “no outbound calls at all” and are confused why installer still needs to reach AWS services. They’re asking if they can run w/ no NAT + no public internet and still have the install work. :eyes: (This is coming off the back of SUP-2197)

Supportbot: SUP-2197 updated by Talia Benson — "Installer cannot pull images in locked-down VPC; customer believes private-only means no egress required".

Markus Klein: Yep, we hit this today on the call. They disabled NAT and also didn’t create endpoints, so `helm` pulls / image pulls fail and the installer preflight is complaining about ECR/S3.

Markus Klein: We should give Support a crisp answer they can paste + point to the doc link.

Irene Choi: +1. “No public egress” is supported, but it’s “no internet gateway/NAT egress” — you still need private connectivity to AWS APIs via VPC endpoints (or a customer-managed centralized egress/proxy if they insist).

Victor Alvarez: For AWS VPC baseline (alpha):
- If `nat_mode = "none"` (or `enable_nat_gateway=false` depending on which example they’re using), then **required** endpoints are:
  - S3 gateway endpoint (for image layers + artifacts)
  - ECR API + ECR DKR interface endpoints (for pulling images)
  - STS interface endpoint (installer/auth flows; also shows up if they’re using assumed roles)
  - CloudWatch Logs interface endpoint (if they enable CW logs destination / preflight checks)
- Optional but common: SSM (if they use SSM Session Manager for bastionless access)

Victor Alvarez: And private DNS needs to be on for the interface endpoints if they want everything to “just work” with standard AWS hostnames.

Bruno Silva: Concrete guidance to send:
1) “Private-only” means no 0.0.0.0/0 route to IGW/NAT from the private/isolated subnets.
2) You must have VPC endpoints for the AWS services the deployment depends on.
3) Ensure endpoint security groups allow 443 from the relevant subnets.
4) Ensure DNS works (VPC DNS hostnames/resolution enabled, plus Route53 resolver if they’ve got custom DNS).

Bruno Silva: Quick checks we used:
- `aws ecr get-login-password --region <region>` from the admin host (fails w/o STS/ECR endpoints)
- `nslookup api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com` (should resolve to private IPs if private DNS enabled)
- `curl -s https://sts.<region>.amazonaws.com` (should connect, even though it’s “private-only”)

Fatima Noor: The phrasing is what trips regulated folks. They often interpret “no egress” as “no outbound network connections of any kind.” We should explicitly say “no public internet egress; AWS PrivateLink/Gateway endpoints still required.”

Talia Benson: Do we have a canonical doc link that states this clearly? Right now Support is pointing at random PR README snippets.

Irene Choi: Use the quickstart + the installer preflight runbook.
- Confluence: AWS VPC Terraform quickstart (alpha) — section “Locked-down / no public egress” + endpoint list
  https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGPRIVATE/pages/128771286/aws-vpc-terraform-quickstart-alpha
- Runbook: Private installer networking preflight checks
  https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLATFORM/pages/129104233/private-installer-networking-preflight-checks

Victor Alvarez: Also the endpoint requirements matrix (internal) if they want rationale per component, but Support probably shouldn’t forward that externally.

Markus Klein: Here’s a pasteable response we can give Support (feel free to tweak):

> Redwood Private supports “no public internet egress” deployments (no NAT/IGW routes from workload subnets). In this mode the environment still needs private connectivity to required AWS services using VPC endpoints (PrivateLink / gateway endpoints). At minimum, S3 gateway + ECR (api+dkr) interface endpoints are required for pulling images and artifacts, and STS is required for auth flows. Ensure private DNS is enabled for interface endpoints and that the endpoint security group allows HTTPS (443) from the Redwood subnets.

Markus Klein: If they need an example, tell them to use the “enterprise locked-down” example tfvars in the alpha examples repo (the one that toggles private-only endpoints / disables NAT). That was designed for exactly this confusion.

Talia Benson: Perfect. I’ll reply to the ticket and update the canned response template for pilot Support.

Talia Benson: Action item on our side: add one callout in the docs that “private-only” != “air-gapped” and explicitly list required endpoints in the quickstart top section.

Irene Choi: :thumbsup: Please tag me on the doc PR if you want wording review.

Bruno Silva: Same — happy to sanity check the endpoint list against what we’ve seen in pilots.

Supportbot: SUP-2197 internal note added by Talia Benson — "Sent guidance: no public egress supported w/ required VPC endpoints + private DNS; linked quickstart + preflight runbook".
